"""
date_range_parser.py

A tiny, dependency‑free parser that turns short English date‑range
descriptions into concrete start/end dates.

Supported description styles (case‑insensitive):

    • "first to the last day of <Month> <Year>"
    • "<Day> to <Day> of <Month> <Year>"
    • "<Day>‑<Day> of <Month> <Year>"
    • "<Month> <Year>"                → whole month
    • "today"                         → (today, today)
    • "yesterday"                     → (yesterday, yesterday)

The returned dates are strings formatted as ISO “YYYY‑MM‑DD”.
If a description cannot be understood, a ``ValueError`` is raised.
"""

import re
import calendar
from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta
from typing import Tuple

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Helper data
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

# Mapping of month names / abbreviations → month number (1‑12)
_MONTHS = {
    "january": 1,   "jan": 1,
    "february": 2,  "feb": 2,
    "march": 3,     "mar": 3,
    "april": 4,     "apr": 4,
    "may": 5,
    "june": 6,      "jun": 6,
    "july": 7,      "jul": 7,
    "august": 8,    "aug": 8,
    "september": 9, "sep": 9, "sept": 9,
    "october": 10,  "oct": 10,
    "november": 11, "nov": 11,
    "december": 12, "dec": 12,
}


def _month_name_to_number(name: str) -> int:
    """Return month number (1‑12) for a given English month name/abbrev."""
    try:
        return _MONTHS[name.lower()]
    except KeyError:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown month name: {name!r}")


def _ordinal_to_int(token: str) -> int:
    """
    Convert an ordinal string (1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, …) or a plain integer
    to an ``int``.
    """
    token = token.lower().strip()
    # Strip the trailing “st/nd/rd/th”
    token = re.sub(r"(st|nd|rd|th)$", "", token)
    if not token.isdigit():
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid day token: {token!r}")
    return int(token)


def _last_day_of_month(year: int, month: int) -> int:
    """Return the last calendar day of the given month."""
    return calendar.monthrange(year, month)[1]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Core parser
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

class DateRangeParser:
    """
    Parse short English descriptions of a date range into concrete dates.

    Example
    -------
    >>> parser = DateRangeParser()
    >>> parser.parse("first to the last day of March 2023")
    ('2023-03-01', '2023-03-31')
    >>> parser.parse("1st‑15th of April 2022")
    ('2022-04-01', '2022-04-15')
    >>> parser.parse("July 2021")
    ('2021-07-01', '2021-07-31')
    """

    # --------------------------------------------------------------- #
    # Regular‑expression patterns (compiled once for speed)
    # --------------------------------------------------------------- #
    _PAT_FIRST_TO_LAST = re.compile(
        r"""^
        (first)\s+to\s+(the\s+)?(last\s+day\s+of)\s+
        (?P<month>\w+)\s+(?P<year>\d{4})
        $""",
        re.IGNORECASE | re.VERBOSE,
    )

    _PAT_DAY_TO_DAY_OF_MONTH = re.compile(
        r"""^
        (?P<day1>\d{1,2}(?:st|nd|rd|th)?)\s*
        (?:to|\-)\s*
        (?P<day2>\d{1,2}(?:st|nd|rd|th)?)\s*
        (?:of|in)\s+
        (?P<month>\w+)\s+(?P<year>\d{4})
        $""",
        re.IGNORECASE | re.VERBOSE,
    )

    _PAT_WHOLE_MONTH = re.compile(
        r"""^
        (?P<month>\w+)\s+(?P<year>\d{4})
        $""",
        re.IGNORECASE | re.VERBOSE,
    )

    _PAT_TODAY = re.compile(r"^today$", re.IGNORECASE)
    _PAT_YESTERDAY = re.compile(r"^yesterday$", re.IGNORECASE)

    # --------------------------------------------------------------- #
    def __init__(self, output_format: str = "%Y-%m-%d"):
        """
        Parameters
        ----------
        output_format: str, optional
            The ``datetime.strftime`` format used for the returned strings.
            Default is ISO‑like ``YYYY‑MM‑DD``.
        """
        self.out_fmt = output_format

    # --------------------------------------------------------------- #
    def _format(self, d: date) -> str:
        """Utility – format a ``date`` according to ``self.out_fmt``."""
        return d.strftime(self.out_fmt)

    # --------------------------------------------------------------- #
    def parse(self, description: str) -> Tuple[str, str]:
        """
        Parse the supplied description and return a ``(start, end)`` tuple.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the description cannot be understood.
        """
        desc = description.strip()
        if not desc:
            raise ValueError("Empty description")

        # 1️⃣  “today” / “yesterday”
        if self._PAT_TODAY.fullmatch(desc):
            today = date.today()
            return self._format(today), self._format(today)

        if self._PAT_YESTERDAY.fullmatch(desc):
            yest = date.today() - timedelta(days=1)
            return self._format(yest), self._format(yest)

        # 2️⃣  “first to the last day of <Month> <Year>”
        m = self._PAT_FIRST_TO_LAST.fullmatch(desc)
        if m:
            month = _month_name_to_number(m.group("month"))
            year = int(m.group("year"))
            start = date(year, month, 1)
            end = date(year, month, _last_day_of_month(year, month))
            return self._format(start), self._format(end)

        # 3️⃣  “<Day> to <Day> of <Month> <Year>”
        m = self._PAT_DAY_TO_DAY_OF_MONTH.fullmatch(desc)
        if m:
            month = _month_name_to_number(m.group("month"))
            year = int(m.group("year"))
            day1 = _ordinal_to_int(m.group("day1"))
            day2 = _ordinal_to_int(m.group("day2"))

            # sanity checks
            max_day = _last_day_of_month(year, month)
            if not (1 <= day1 <= max_day and 1 <= day2 <= max_day):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Day out of range for {month}/{year}: {day1}-{day2}"
                )
            if day1 > day2:
                raise ValueError("Start day is greater than end day")

            start = date(year, month, day1)
            end = date(year, month, day2)
            return self._format(start), self._format(end)

        # 4️⃣  “<Month> <Year>” → whole month
        m = self._PAT_WHOLE_MONTH.fullmatch(desc)
        if m:
            month = _month_name_to_number(m.group("month"))
            year = int(m.group("year"))
            start = date(year, month, 1)
            end = date(year, month, _last_day_of_month(year, month))
            return self._format(start), self._format(end)

        # ----------------------------------------------------------- #
        raise ValueError(f"Could not parse date‑range description: {desc!r}")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Simple manual test / demo (executed only when running the file directly)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = DateRangeParser()
    demo_cases = [
        "first to the last day of March 2023",

        except ValueError as exc:

```

    # Public API
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------------

        self,

#!/usr/bin/env python
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-

"""
date_range_parser.py

A tiny natural‑language date‑range parser.

Supported phrases (case‑insensitive, whitespace tolerant):

  * "first to last day of a month"
  * "first day of <month> [<year>]"
  * "last day of <month> [<year>]"
  * "today", "yesterday", "tomorrow"
  * "last N days", "next N days"
  * "from YYYY‑MM‑DD to YYYY‑MM‑DD"
  * "last week", "this week", "next week"
  * "last month", "this month", "next month"

The parser returns a 2‑tuple of ISO‑8601 strings (YYYY‑MM‑DD) that
represent the start and end of the requested range.

Author: ChatGPT – 2024
"""

import re
import calendar
from datetime import datetime, date, timedelta
from typing import Tuple, Optional, Callable, List, Pattern

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper functions – pure date arithmetic (no external libs except dateutil)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
from dateutil.relativedelta import relativedelta


def _as_date(d: datetime | date) -> date:
    """Coerce datetime → date, leave date unchanged."""
    return d.date() if isinstance(d, datetime) else d


def first_day(dt: date) -> date:
    """First day (00:00) of the month that contains *dt*."""
    return dt.replace(day=1)


def last_day(dt: date) -> date:
    """Last calendar day of the month that contains *dt*."""
    last = calendar.monthrange(dt.year, dt.month)[1]
    return dt.replace(day=last)


def monday_of_week(dt: date) -> date:
    """Monday of the ISO week that contains *dt*."""
    return dt - timedelta(days=dt.weekday())  # Monday == 0


def sunday_of_week(dt: date) -> date:
    """Sunday of the ISO week that contains *dt*."""
    return dt + timedelta(days=(6 - dt.weekday()))  # Sunday == 6


def month_name_to_number(name: str) -> int:
    """'January' → 1, case‑insensitive, also accepts 3‑letter abbrevs."""
    try:
        return datetime.strptime(name[:3], "%b").month
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown month name: {name}") from exc


def _today(reference: Optional[date] = None) -> date:
    """Return *reference* if supplied, otherwise today's date (UTC)."""
    return reference if reference is not None else datetime.utcnow().date()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Core parser class
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
class DateRangeParser:
    """
    Parse a limited set of natural‑language date‑range specifications.
    """

    # -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Regex → handler mapping
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Each entry is a tuple (pattern, handler).  The handler receives the
    # re.Match object and a reference date, and must return a (start, end)
    # tuple of ``date`` objects.
    _PATTERNS: List[Tuple[Pattern, Callable[[re.Match, date], Tuple[date, date]]]] = []

    @classmethod
    def _register(cls, pattern: str):
        """
        Decorator used to register a new regex → handler pair.
        ``pattern`` must be a *raw* regex string (case‑insensitive).
        """

        def wrapper(func: Callable[[re.Match, date], Tuple[date, date]]):
            compiled = re.compile(pattern, re.IGNORECASE)
            cls._PATTERNS.append((compiled, func))
            return func

        return wrapper

    # -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Individual pattern handlers
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------------

    @_register(r"^\s*first\s+to\s+last\s+day\s+of\s+a\s+month\s*$")
    def _handle_first_to_last_month(match: re.Match, ref: date) -> Tuple[date, date]:
        """'first to last day of a month' → whole current month."""
        start = first_day(ref)
        end = last_day(ref)
        return start, end

    @_register(
        r"^\s*first\s+day\s+of\s+(?P<month>\w+)(?:\s+(?P<year>\d{4}))?\s*$"
    )
    def _handle_first_day_of_month(match: re.Match, ref: date) -> Tuple[date, date]:
        """'first day of May 2023' → May 1 2023."""
        month = month_name_to_number(match.group("month"))
        year = int(match.group("year")) if match.group("year") else ref.year
        start = date(year, month, 1)
        return start, start

    @_register(
        r"^\s*last\s+day\s+of\s+(?P<month>\w+)(?:\s+(?P<year>\d{4}))?\s*$"
    )
    def _handle_last_day_of_month(match: re.Match, ref: date) -> Tuple[date, date]:
        """'last day of february' → Feb 28/29 of the relevant year."""
        month = month_name_to_number(match.group("month"))
        year = int(match.group("year")) if match.group("year") else ref.year
        last = calendar.monthrange(year, month)[1]
        dt = date(year, month, last)
        return dt, dt

    @_register(r"^\s*today\s*$")
    def _handle_today(match: re.Match, ref: date) -> Tuple[date, date]:
        return ref, ref

    @_register(r"^\s*yesterday\s*$")
    def _handle_yesterday(match: re.Match, ref: date) -> Tuple[date, date]:
        d = ref - timedelta(days=1)
        return d, d

    @_register(r"^\s*tomorrow\s*$")
    def _handle_tomorrow(match: re.Match, ref: date) -> Tuple[date, date]:
        d = ref + timedelta(days=1)
        return d, d

    @_register(r"^\s*last\s+(?P<num>\d+)\s+days\s*$")
    def _handle_last_n_days(match: re.Match, ref: date) -> Tuple[date, date]:
        n = int(match.group("num"))
        start = ref - timedelta(days=n - 1)  # inclusive range
        return start, ref

    @_register(r"^\s*next\s+(?P<num>\d+)\s+days\s*$")
    def _handle_next_n_days(match: re.Match, ref: date) -> Tuple[date, date]:
        n = int(match.group("num"))
        end = ref + timedelta(days=n - 1)
        return ref, end

    @_register(
        r"^\s*from\s+(?P<start>\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})\s+to\s+(?P<end>\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})\s*$"
    )
    def _handle_from_to(match: re.Match, ref: date) -> Tuple[date, date]:
        start = datetime.strptime(match.group("start"), "%Y-%m-%d").date()
        end = datetime.strptime(match.group("end"), "%Y-%m-%d").date()
        if start > end:
            raise ValueError("Start date must be ≤ end date")
        return start, end

    @_register(r"^\s*last\s+week\s*$")
    def _handle_last_week(match: re.Match, ref: date) -> Tuple[date, date]:
        # week = Monday … Sunday (ISO style).  "Last week" means the week
        # before the current ISO week.
        this_monday = monday_of_week(ref)
        start = this_monday - timedelta(weeks=1)
        end = start + timedelta(days=6)
        return start, end

    @_register(r"^\s*this\s+week\s*$")
    def _handle_this_week(match: re.Match, ref: date) -> Tuple[date, date]:
        start = monday_of_week(ref)
        end = start + timedelta(days=6)
        return start, end

    @_register(r"^\s*next\s+week\s*$")
    def _handle_next_week(match: re.Match, ref: date) -> Tuple[date, date]:
        start = monday_of_week(ref) + timedelta(weeks=1)
        end = start + timedelta(days=6)
        return start, end

    @_register(r"^\s*last\s+month\s*$")
    def _handle_last_month(match: re.Match, ref: date) -> Tuple[date, date]:
        dt = (ref.replace(day=1) - relativedelta(months=1))
        return first_day(dt), last_day(dt)

    @_register(r"^\s*this\s+month\s*$")
    def _handle_this_month(match: re.Match, ref: date) -> Tuple[date, date]:
        return first_day(ref), last_day(ref)

    @_register(r"^\s*next\s+month\s*$")
    def _handle_next_month(match: re.Match, ref: date) -> Tuple[date, date]:
        dt = (ref.replace(day=1) + relativedelta(months=1))
        return first_day(dt), last_day(dt)

    # -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Public API
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    def parse(
        self,
        text: str,
        *,
        reference: Optional[date] = None,
        output_format: str = "%Y-%m-%d",
    ) -> Tuple[str, str]:
        """
        Parse *text* and return a tuple ``(start_str, end_str)`` formatted
        with *output_format* (default ISO‑8601).

        Parameters
        ----------
        text:
            The natural‑language description to parse.
        reference:
            A date used as “today”.  Supplying a value makes unit‑testing
            deterministic.  If omitted, UTC today is used.
        output_format:
            ``datetime.strftime`` format string for the result.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If no pattern matches or the phrase is malformed.
        """
        ref = _today(reference)

        for pat, handler in self._PATTERNS:
            m = pat.fullmatch(text)
            if m:
                start_dt, end_dt = handler(m, ref)
                # Defensive sanity‑check
                if start_dt > end_dt:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"Handler for pattern {pat.pattern} produced invalid range "
                        f"{start_dt} > {end_dt}"
                    )
                return (start_dt.strftime(output_format), end_dt.strftime(output_format))

        raise ValueError(f"Unable to parse date range description: {text!r}")

    # -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Utility: expose the list of known patterns (helpful for debugging)
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    @classmethod
    def known_patterns(cls) -> List[str]:
        """Return the raw regex strings that the parser understands."""
        return [pat.pattern for pat, _ in cls._PATTERNS]

from date_range_parser import DateRangeParser


class TestDateRangeParser(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.parser = DateRangeParser()
        # Use a deterministic "today" for all tests
        self.ref = date(2023, 5, 17)   # a Wednesday

    def test_first_to_last_month(self):
        start, end = self.parser.parse("first to last day of a month", reference=self.ref)
        self.assertEqual(start, "2023-05-01")
        self.assertEqual(end, "2023-05-31")

    def test_first_day_of_month_with_year(self):
        start, end = self.parser.parse("first day of february 2022")
